dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvaṃ dehaṃ cinmayaṃ hi jagad vā paribhāvayet | yugapan nirvikalpena manasā paramodayaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one contemplate the whole body, or the world, as made of consciousness, all at once and with a mind free of thought-constructs; then comes the supreme awakening.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh stresses two conditions: an unwavering mind free of doubts and alternatives (nirvikalpena manasā), and simultaneity (yugapat), in one sweep, not piece by piece. The supreme awakening is the recognition that the whole universe is enveloped in divine light.
dharana.technique_name: Body and World as Consciousness, All at Once
dharana.instruction: Take in your whole body, then the world, in one sweep, as made of awareness.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 63 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the whole body, or the whole world, taken in one sweep as made of awareness.
geometry.svg_hint: a body outline and a wide circle around it, both filled with the same even light
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: One sweep
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention that moves piece by piece takes in the whole at once, as awareness. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Take in the whole body, or the whole world, in one sweep
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The whole body or world contemplated as consciousness, all at once

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one contemplate the whole body, or the world, as made of consciousness, all at once and with a mind free of thought-constructs; then comes the supreme awakening.
adiyogi.method_summary: Take in the whole body in one sweep, not part by part, as made of awareness. If that is clear, widen to the whole world. Hold it with a steady, unhesitating mind.

honesty.disclosure: Door 040 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 40 (verse 63) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 040 is dharana 40, verse 63. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If one sweep is not possible, start with a small region and widen slowly. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 040: body and world as consciousness, all at once. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 40, verse 63.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down. The map is the whole body and the whole world, in one sweep.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Take in the whole body at once as awareness. Then the whole world. One sweep. A steady mind.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: piece-by-piece attention becoming one sweep. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 63: contemplate the whole body or the world as consciousness, all at once and thought-free; then comes the supreme awakening.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.
